advances: Necessary centroid restrictions in the one-positive-row stratum of the auxiliary objective.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
The partial-zero-row exclusion applies because the full row provides funding, so the remaining nonzero rows have one zero. The boundary-multiplier identities apply because the full row has a proper minimum and the matrix is a positive-weight local maximizer. Rows with the same zero column have equal weights and positive entries proportional to the same reciprocal-multiplier vector. Their sum therefore has capacity equal to the sum of their capacities by homogeneity of the geometric mean, and its scale is the sum of their scales. The merger preserves the objective and all column sums. Distinct remaining zero columns can be placed at the corresponding diagonal positions by a column permutation, which just permutes the entries of $x$, $b$ and $\lambda$.

In column $j$ the remaining mass $1-x_j$ is the sum of the entries $\mu_i/\lambda_j$ over surviving rows $i\ne j$. This yields $\lambda_j(1-x_j)=\mu-\mu_j$. For the sole positive row the section-gradient equations give $b=\lambda/S$, $t=x\cdot b$, and $c_r\phi_d(x)=St$. Indeed its capacity vector cannot be a standard unit vector, since $0<\phi_d(x)=t/F_x(t)^{1/d}<1$: a proper minimum is strictly smaller than the ratio $\max_j x_j\le1$ at the full threshold by uniqueness. For each surviving one-zero row its contribution is $d\mu_i$, which also equals the pairing of its entries with $\lambda$. Thus the objective is the sum of the row pairings with $\lambda$, hence $S$ by column stochasticity. It equals $St+d\mu$, giving the formula for $\mu$. Properness and $0<x_j\le1$ yield $0<t<1$.

For each point $u$ of the section, $\sum_j (1-x_j)u_j=1-t$, so the stated map sends it to $\Delta_d$. Taking its centroid by linearity of expectation gives the expression in the statement; substituting the column identity shows equality exactly when $\mu_j=0$. Even if $x_j=1$, that coordinate can simply be mapped to zero.

source_sections.locator: §5, (8)–(9), matched row merger and actual section pushforward

statement:
For $d\ge1$, let $U$ be uniform on $\Delta_d=\{u\in\mathbb R_+^{d+1}:\sum_j u_j=1\}$, and for $x\ge0$ put $F_x(t)=\Pr(x\cdot U\le t)$ and $\phi_d(x)=\inf_{t>0:F_x(t)>0} t/F_x(t)^{1/d}$. Assume $d\ge2$. Let $X$ be a local maximizer of $H(X)=\sum_i c_i\phi_d(X_i)$ over nonnegative column-stochastic $(d+1)\times(d+1)$ matrices, where $X_i$ is row $i$ and every $c_i>0$. Suppose exactly one row $r$ is strictly positive, with a proper minimizing threshold $t$. Write $x=X_r$, $b$ for its actual section centroid, $\lambda=c_r\nabla\phi_d(x)$ and $S=\sum_j\lambda_j$. Group the nonzero rows other than $r$ by their unique zero column, and replace each group by its sum in one of its own row labels, setting the other rows in that group to zero. Permute columns to place each surviving such row's zero on its diagonal. After this relabeling, let $\mu_i=c_i\phi_d(X_i)/d$ for each surviving row other than $r$, and set $\mu_i=0$ at unmatched labels including $r$. Write $\mu=\sum_i\mu_i$. The merger preserves the objective and gives
$$
H(X)=S,\qquad b=\lambda/S,\qquad
0<t=x\cdot b<1,\qquad
\lambda_j(1-x_j)=\mu-\mu_j,\qquad
\mu=\frac{S(1-t)}d .
$$
The image of the actual section measure under $u_j\mapsto (1-x_j)u_j/(1-t)$ is a probability on $\Delta_d$ whose $j$th centroid coordinate is
$$
\frac{(1-x_j)b_j}{1-t}=\frac1d-\frac{\mu_j}{S(1-t)}\le\frac1d.
$$
Equality holds exactly at unmatched labels. The pushforward statement includes collapsed coordinates.
title: Rescaled section centroid with exactly one positive row
